replay.compare: mixdog-app-server thread feed batching: replay the steps against the Rust mailbox on a virtual clock; compare the frames (sequence, value, critical) and pending-timer counts after every step, and for the encoder cases the wires
replay.entry: NO RUST ENTRY: in K1 the phone is a protocol connection of the core (mixdog-app-server-transport/src/relay.rs) that reads the thread feed; the relay writer (mixdog-app-server-transport/src/writer.rs) sends every feed frame in order and batches none. The phone's frame publication is being changed on branch phone-chat-live (session actor thread/frame, mixdog-core-session session/phone_frame.rs), which is where a 90 ms text batch for the phone belongs; its five frame cases go with that branch. The partial-append parity case is replayed on its desktop half (apps/desktop/src/shared/streaming-partial-replay.test.mjs); the old-decoder case is not applicable (see cases).

cases.the desktop and daemon partial-append su: replayed, desktop half: apps/desktop/src/shared/streaming-partial-replay.test.mjs runs K1's only maker of the patch (ipc-state-bridge.ts:175 createSnapshotDeltaEncoder({partialAppend}) → state-delta.ts:583 streamingPartialSuffix, desktop main → renderer) over every recorded input and compares the `desktop` answers. Daemon half not applicable: the core makes no snapshot patch; a growing line reaches a client as item/agentMessage/delta (packages/protocol-client/src/session-state.ts:207), so session-state-patch.mjs has no K1 counterpart
